problem: In one session, changing normalized features below the matching threshold created new tracks that bypassed the intended greeting cooldown, even while one face remained continuously visible.
behavior: Valid face vectors retain aligned optional RAM-only normalized boxes; features() remains vector-only and compatible
Strong embedding matches are reserved first; unique recent overlap can mark temporary unknown-greeting continuity
Suppression rechecks the original anchor, current overlap, ambiguity, age and separately visible original face at greeting time
Current embeddings still supply recognized names; independent known-name cooldowns prevent drift from bypassing the existing120-second intent
No new enrollment, persistent boxes, raw images, identity assignment or changes to user-requested speech

tests.baseline: Controlled normalized A/B/C vectors produced3 introductions for one continuous face in both unknown and same-known-name cases

independent_correction.meaning: Both detection orders after occlusion, moved geometry and newly ambiguous overlap retain new visitor greetings

actual_cpu_video_qualification.source: Owner-provided clip, same transient observations supplied to baseline and candidate
actual_cpu_video_qualification.models: Existing pinned OpenCV YuNet/SFace on CPU
actual_cpu_video_qualification.claim: Compatibility on one stable single-person clip, not measured drift improvement or general recognition accuracy

limits: Unknown people replacing one another in the same position without an observed absence remain ambiguous and may share presentation continuity
Greeting memory is session-local; restarting the camera can introduce Cale again
Geometry only affects automatic greeting presentation, never identity recognition, enrollment or access
No live webcam, multiple-person video, new GPU/frame-rate, fresh-PC or full installed self-check qualification in this release
Optional dependency snapshot prototype and expression-helper port are not included
